newsitem.title: UK: Ldn palladium hits fresh 21-month high, slips later.
newsitem.headline: Ldn palladium hits fresh 21-month high, slips later.

text.p: The palladium price climbed to a fresh 21-month high at its 0845 fixing on Thursday as worries over supply gripped the market, dealers said.
The concern in palladium stems from major supplier Russia's administrative snarl-up which has stopped exports since last November. The price has increased by 40 percent since then.
Palladium fixed at $160.25 per ounce, its highst fix since July 28, 1995 and $3.25 above its Wednesday afternoon fix.
However after the fix a statement from a Russian ministry of Finance official that shipments to Japan -- the major consumer of the metal -- could begin in May knocked $6.00 off the price.
"This is an event-driven thing," said one market analyst.
The rare white metal is used in electronic components and is a key element in the catalytic converters which neutralise noxious gases in car exhausts.

"Being short in palladium has been very dangerous but when this thing is resolved, it could get very ugly," one dealer said referrring to the amount of speculative positions which have been taken against the shortfall in Russian supply and the conseqeunt tightness in the market.
Whether or not the market price has been manipulated higher was unclear, despite some dealer opinion that it had.
The U.S.-based Tiger Fund, a cash-rich investment fund, has made high profile announcements that it has bought palladium and expects the price to soar.
"Talking about manipulation in palladium is less paranoid than talking about it in gold because it is a much smaller market," said precious metals analyst Andy Smith at Union bank of Switzerland.
"But it would take somebody of super intelligence to create a successful exit strategy," Smith added, referring to the need to sell a huge holding in the metal without wrecking the price.
Gold, silver and platinum reacted modestly to palladium.
Gold fixed at $348.05, up just 35 cents and it slipped no more than 50 cents when palladium had its mid-moring tumble.
Silver was in a narrow unchanged to two-cents easier range at $4.76/$4.78 and platinum was 25 cents easier at $366.75/$367.75.
Smith noted that the feeling in New York seemed to be much more weighed towards the other precious metals following palladium than it was in the Far East.
"I don't see (palladium price moves) crossing the species barrier," he said.
